summary.headline: AJAX Q1 FY27 revenue rose just 1.7% to INR475 crore and EBITDA fell to INR59 crore, with margin at 12.5%, while SLCM share hit 75.1%.
summary.overview: Total revenue grew 1.7% YoY to INR475 crore, with SLCM flat, non-SLCM up 6.4% to about INR48 crore, and spares and services up 6.2% to INR39 crore. EBITDA fell to INR59 crore from INR61 crore, with margin down 70 bps to 12.5%, and PAT rose 5% to INR55.6 crore. Management said industry SLCM registrations fell 27% and AJAX volumes fell 21%, so the share gain was the main positive. Management guided Q2 as seasonally soft and a challenging margin quarter, with a calibrated price hike under consideration and H2 expected to be better.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR61 crore in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: exceeding INR1,100 crore as of June 2026

segments.name: SLCM (self-loading concrete mixers)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR388 crore, marginally up YoY on favourable mix and the Q4 FY26 price hike. Volumes were about 129 machines across the non-SLCM and SLCM range; management said UDAAN sold 121 units in Q1 and about 35-40 units in June, with 202 units sold last year.

segments.name: Non-SLCM (pumps, batching plants, boom placers)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR48 crore, up 6.4% YoY led by concrete pumps. Non-SLCM volumes were about 129 machines in Q1 FY27 vs about 153 in Q1 FY26, with management citing rain-related deferrals into August-September.

segments.name: Spares and services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR39 crore, up 6.2% YoY on a growing installed base. Management is prioritising a higher AMC share, but gave no quantified target.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: 9% of Q1 revenue. Algeria, Morocco and Nigeria are about 38% of shipments. First slip-form paver exported in the quarter; management guided about 30% CAGR over three years, if not more.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 expected to be seasonally soft and a fairly challenging quarter for margins; 12.5% EBITDA margin looks challenging for Q2.
Margins expected to return to about 12.5% from Q3 if volumes improve; management said 12% full-year looks challenging.
Around 60% of revenue typically comes in H2 (40-60 H1-H2 split); H2 expected to be better than H1 but full-year volume call deferred.
Non-SLCM growth target of 10-15% YoY on a lower base for FY27; H2 expected to be better than H1.
Export business expected to grow at about 30% CAGR over the next three years, if not more.
Calibrated price hike under evaluation, with some actions possibly starting within Q2; ARGO 4000 launch planned in Q2 FY27.
Long-term EBITDA margin corridor of 13-15% stated; Q4 FY26 margin was about 15%.
capex_capacity: Planned ARGO 4000 launch in Q2 FY27 to fill a portfolio gap.
First slip-form paver exported in Q1 FY27; export interest in Africa and Southeast Asia.
Inorganic opportunities being pursued actively; management did not name a target or size.
Strategic inventory built in the first months of FY27 for products with imported components; no large strategic steel purchase made at current prices.
demand_pricing: Industry SLCM registrations fell 27% in Q1 FY27 and AJAX registrations fell 21%; AJAX SLCM and retail share rose to 75.1% from about 69% in Q1 FY26 and 73.5% in FY26.

State-level: Gujarat volumes up 40% with share from 71% to 82%; Rajasthan volumes down 21% with share 66% to 86%; Odisha share 61% to 88%; Chhattisgarh volumes down 11% with share 73% to 91%; Maharashtra and MP volumes down sharply (MP about 50%) despite share gains.
Application mix: urban infra about 15-20% and buildings 10-15%, which management said has risen toward 35-40% combined; roads about 40-43%.
Price increase of about 2% taken in Q4 FY26; another calibrated hike being evaluated. Steel E250 and E350 prices have risen, with some softening expected after September-November.
Competitive pressure from peers selling old CEV 4 inventory in Q1 FY26 cited as a prior-year headwind; ACE and Escorts (pick-and-carry cranes) cited as strong in their segment.

qa_highlights.question: State-wise demand outlook and full-year recovery (Nuvama)
qa_highlights.answer: Gujarat, Odisha, Karnataka and AP are expected to grow; UP has an election-driven upside. Maharashtra and MP show no green shoots yet. Management said government-spend shortfalls have muted the traditional irrigation, railway and power segments.

qa_highlights.question: Non-SLCM growth quantification (Edelweiss)
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 10-15% growth on a lower base would be a decent outcome for non-SLCM this year, with H2 expected to be better than H1.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year SLCM volume growth (JM Financial)
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to call full-year volumes and that H2 is expected to bring improvement; margin pressure from geopolitics, commodities and currency is not expected to ease soon.

qa_highlights.question: Other expenses up about 17% on flat revenue (Bandhan AMC)
qa_highlights.answer: Ketan Pendse attributed the rise to higher outward freight from diesel prices and export mix, plus about INR16 million of SAP ECC 6 to HANA migration cost for this year.

qa_highlights.question: Margin path and Q2 outlook (Citi)
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 will be challenging at about 12.5% margin; Q3 onward is expected to recover to about 12.5% with volume recovery and price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Path back to 15% EBITDA margin (Solidarity Advisors)
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to Q4 FY26 margin of about 15% as proof of capability at higher volumes and set a 13-15% longer-term corridor, subject to demand recovery and calibrated pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Inorganic growth and cash deployment (ICICI Securities)
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is aggressively pursuing inorganic opportunities under set guardrails and will update when it has clarity; no specifics given.

risks_watch: Government infra spending below budget and delayed contractor payments from some states weighing on SLCM demand.
Margin pressure in Q2 from higher steel and diesel costs, with management guiding Q2 as challenging.
Revenue recognition timing for exports and the pace of the calibrated price hike.
Maharashtra and MP volume declines continuing into H2; no recovery signs yet.
Management said it expects 2H pricing to be tested and H2 volume recovery is not yet visible.
Audio quality issues during the call; some analysts reported echo or muffled audio, which may affect the transcript.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on near term: management repeatedly flagged weak government spending, Q2 margin pressure and no volume call for full year. Confident on long-term growth, market share and the H2 recovery, citing the 75.1% share and the 10-year CAGR of about 16-17%.
key_quotes: Our SLCM and retail market share expanded to 75.1% during Q1 FY27, increasing from about 69% in Q1 FY26 and 73.5% during the full year FY26.
Definitely 12.5%, looks challenging at this point in time from a second quarter perspective.
I think it's too early for us to make a call on the full-year numbers at this stage.
we are not playing the price game, we would rather play the installation game even if it means that it is a little tougher to do.

adds.what: ARGO 4000 product launch (new product, not stated as capacity addition)

growth.why: Management guides non-SLCM growth of 10-15% for FY27 on a lower base, a 30% export CAGR over three years, and margins back to about 12.5% from Q3, backed mainly by share gains, a price hike under evaluation and the ARGO 4000 launch, with no quantified capacity or order book behind them; Q2 is guided as seasonally soft and challenging.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin fell 70 bps to 12.5% in Q1 and Q2 is guided as challenging at about 12.5%; recovery to about 12.5% from Q3 depends on volume recovery and a calibrated price hike still under evaluation, with Q4 FY26 at about 15% as the reference point.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant, line or capacity was discussed; the ARGO 4000 is a product launch to fill a portfolio gap, and the only capacity-like item is an export slip-form paver already shipped.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AJAX SLCM volumes fell 21% and industry registrations fell 27% in Q1, with management calling full-year volumes too early to call and H2 recovery not yet visible; non-SLCM is guided at 10-15% growth on a lower base.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed and no new capex was discussed; management only mentioned inorganic opportunities with no size or target, and strategic inventory build rather than capacity build.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management described Q2 as seasonally soft and challenging, said 12% full-year margin looks challenging, and deferred the full-year volume call, so no upgrade signal.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 margin guided challenging at about 12.5%, Maharashtra and MP show no green shoots, government spending has muted irrigation, railway and power, and steel and diesel costs remain elevated.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: ARGO 4000 launch is planned in Q2 FY27 to fill a portfolio gap, and the first slip-form paver was exported in Q1 FY27 with export growth guided at about 30% CAGR.

rows.label: Calibrated price hike under evaluation
rows.why: A second calibrated hike is being evaluated after a about 2% increase in Q4 FY26, with some actions possibly starting in Q2, but steel E250/E350 prices may soften after September-November.

rows.label: Export growth to Africa and Southeast Asia
rows.why: Exports were 9% of Q1 revenue, Algeria, Morocco and Nigeria are about 38% of shipments, and management guided about 30% CAGR over three years, if not more.

rows.label: Inorganic acquisition
rows.why: Management is aggressively pursuing inorganic opportunities under set guardrails with over INR1,100 crore cash, but gave no target or size and said it will update when it has clarity.
